Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

isolate verb

also isolated, isolation, keep apart, set apart, cut off, quarantine

classical

Phaedr. 3.15.3: ovēsque sēgregātās
Cic. Arch. 4: nōn modo nōn sēgregandum ā numerō cīvium (Lewis & Short)

sēgregō, sēgregāre, sēgregāvī, sēgregātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive; ab + abl.

set apart, separate, isolate

From grex: to take out of the flock, and so to set anyone or anything apart from the rest (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • sēcernō, sēcernere, sēcrēvī, sēcrētum — separate, sort out, set apart

    verb, third conjugation, transitive; ab + abl. · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 1.32: mūrō dēnique sēcernantur ā nōbīs (Lewis & Short); Col. 12.50.1

    To part one thing from another, as bad olives from good (Columella) or the conspirators from the city.

  • sēclūdō, sēclūdere, sēclūsī, sēclūsum — shut away, confine apart

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Varr. RR 2.2.8: incientēs (ovēs) sēclūdere (Lewis & Short)

    Rare but classical (Lewis & Short): to shut up in a place of its own, as Varro the ewes about to lamb. An isolated place is sōlitārius or dēvius.

Examples

  • inter capellās agnō bālantī canis: stulte, inquit, errās; nōn est hīc māter tua; ovēsque sēgregātās ostendit procul

    to a lamb bleating among the she-goats a dog said: “Silly, you’re wrong; your mother isn’t here,” and pointed to the sheep, kept apart some way offPhaedr. 3.15.1–3

  • Ovem aegram ā cēterīs sēgregā, nē morbus serpat.

    Keep the sick sheep away from the others, so the illness doesn’t spread.composed

See also separate, alone, exclude.
